shape.def: The overall form of a quantitative distribution on a graph: whether it is symmetric or skewed, how many peaks it has, or whether it is level (uniform).

symmetric.def: A distribution whose left and right sides are roughly mirror images of each other around its center.

skewed.def: A distribution with a long tail on one side. It is skewed right when the tail stretches toward larger values, skewed left when the tail stretches toward smaller values.

modality.def: The number of peaks (modes) in a distribution: unimodal has one, bimodal has two, multimodal has more.

uniform-shape.def: A distribution in which all values occur about equally often, so its histogram has bars of about the same height.

center.def: A typical or middle value of a distribution, around which the data are located.

spread.def: Variability: how far apart the values of a distribution are from each other, or how much they vary.

outlier.def: A value that falls far from the overall pattern of a distribution. It should be investigated, not simply removed.

gap-cluster.def: A gap is a stretch of the number line with no values; a cluster is a bunch of values set apart from the rest by gaps.
